conventions.convention: Geometric cancellation requires consecutive handles and exactly one transverse attaching-belt intersection. Indices 0 and n−1 have explicit endpoint conventions; an algebraic unit alone does not establish this condition.
Slides are defined for 1 ≤ k ≤ dim(W)−2, with framed band data. The index-one case replaces one attaching point using the other endpoint of the second attaching zero-sphere.

The attaching-belt matrix has upper handles in rows and lower handles in columns. The differential acts on row coordinates by x ↦ xM; its column-coordinate matrix is Mᵀ. A lower core change c_j′ ↦ c_j′ + εc_j changes column j by C_j ↦ C_j−εC_j′.

Morse cancellation localizes the replacement vector field in the prescribed trajectory neighbourhood. The replacement function agrees near the slab faces, but need not agree outside that neighbourhood.
χ(M) is the alternating sum of rational Betti numbers, with χ(∅)=0. Compact manifolds with boundary are included; finiteness is discharged by a proposition assuming full AC.
For a balanced oriented finite zero-manifold, reduced degree is one half of the signed sum of its ±1 values. On S⁰ it is (f(+1)−f(−1))/2.
Local vector-field index is defined for n ≥ 1, using reduced degree when n=1. Base and fibre orientations must match; chart changes alter both signs, so no global orientation is needed.
The positive Morse gradient contributes (−1)^λ; the negative gradient contributes (−1)^(n−λ). Negating an arbitrary field multiplies its local index by (−1)^n.
The zero-section intersection is ordered I(X₀,Γ_X), with the ambient tangent-bundle orientation horizontal first, vertical second.
Boundary Poincare-Hopf requires strict outwardness, not merely a nonzero boundary field. Its boundary clause is vacuous for empty boundary.
The reflected field uses the collar generated by −X to define the double. Reflection followed by negation is smooth in that collar; an arbitrary fixed collar need not work.
An h-cobordism has total dimension n+1 ≥ 2 and both actual boundary inclusions are homotopy equivalences. The definition is symmetric and does not assume simple connectivity or orientation.

Trading requires a full framed attaching embedding in the common part of two levels, plus framed isotopies to single-belt position and to a standard trivial embedding one level higher. Core nullhomotopy alone is insufficient.

The arbitrary-sphere homology lemma covers 2 ≤ q ≤ n−3. At q=2 it additionally requires injectivity from the incoming fundamental group to the trace. The flipped q=n−2 endpoint is proved separately for actual h-cobordism handle spheres.
The smooth simply connected theorem assumes boundary dimension n ≥ 5 and countable choice. The punctured-contractible-manifold corollary assumes full AC for its duality, UCT and Hurewicz suppliers.

load_bearing.statement: Assume countable choice. For a compact collared smooth n-manifold W, a k-handle followed by a (k+1)-handle, 0 ≤ k ≤ n−1, cancels relative to the incoming boundary if the upper attaching sphere meets the lower belt sphere transversely in exactly one point. Later attaching data are transported by the diffeomorphism.

Assume countable choice. Full attaching embeddings into the boundary of a compact smooth manifold, extending over a neighbourhood of the disk factor and joined by a smooth isotopy stationary near its time endpoints, give diffeomorphic rounded attachments. The comparison is supported in a collar of the swept regions and transports later attaching data.

Assume countable choice. For a finite index-ordered handle decomposition of a compact collared triad relative to M₀, C_k=H_k(W_k,W_(k−1);Z), with the triple connecting differential, is free on the core classes, has differential squared zero, and computes H_k(W,M₀;Z). With the specified oriented core/belt conventions its coefficients are attaching-belt intersection numbers; the upper-row/lower-column matrix acts on row coordinates.

Assume countable choice. For a finite presentation relative to a closed connected incoming n-manifold, n ≥ 5, with all indices at least q, 2 ≤ q ≤ n−2, the complement of all or any subfamily of the q-handle belts induces a fundamental-group isomorphism to the outgoing q-level, provided at q=2 the incoming fundamental-group map to the trace is injective. For q=2 the stated opposite-sign null-Whitney-circle configuration admits a clean framed disk avoiding the other belts and prescribed additional disjoint two-spheres.

Assume countable choice. In a compact (n+1)-dimensional index-ordered presentation with all indices at least q, 1 ≤ q ≤ n−2, let α be a framed S^q×D^(n−q) attachment in the common part of the q- and (q+1)-levels. If α is framed-isotopic in the q-level to meeting one selected q-belt once and all others not at all, and framed-isotopic in the next level to a standard trivial embedding in an n-disk, that q-handle can be deleted and one (q+2)-handle added, preserving all other handle counts and the manifold relative to its incoming face.

Assume countable choice. A connected h-cobordism of dimension n+1, n ≥ 5, with closed simply connected faces admits, for every 2 ≤ k ≤ n−2, an index-ordered presentation using only k- and (k+1)-handles, with equally many of each and two-term integral relative differential an isomorphism.

Assume countable choice. In the stated handle filtration, the relative core classes form a free integral basis. Under the slide comparison, the slid core has class [C₁′]=[C₁]±[C₂], so a slide is an elementary basis change.

Assume countable choice. A connected simply connected h-cobordism of dimension n+1 ≥ 6 with a two-index presentation k,k+1, 2 ≤ k ≤ n−2, and transverse middle matrix I_r admits attaching-embedding isotopies giving exactly one intersection on each diagonal pair and no off-diagonal intersections, with the same handles.
Assume countable choice for the canonical tangent-bundle structure. On a smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 1, a nondegenerate zero p has local index sign det(DX_p), hence +1 or −1.

Assume countable choice. For a compact full-dimensional smooth domain N⊂R^m, m ≥ 1, and a smooth field with isolated zeros and nonzero boundary values, its index sum equals the componentwise degree of its normalized boundary map, using reduced degree for m=1. If the field is strictly outward, this is the Gauss-map degree.

Assume AC. For a closed smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 1, and a smooth vector field with only isolated zeros, the sum of local indices equals χ(M), componentwise for disconnected M and with zero contribution from the empty zero set.

Assume AC. Compact smooth n-manifolds, possibly with boundary, have finite rational homology vanishing above n. For the stated finite relative CW model, χ(M)−χ(A) equals both the alternating relative cell count and relative Betti sum. For a compact smooth gluing M=M₁∪_N M₂ with both inclusions of N cofibrations, χ(M)=χ(M₁)+χ(M₂)−χ(N).

Assume AC. For a compact smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 1, a smooth field with only isolated zeros, nonzero and strictly outward along the boundary, has index sum χ(M). The boundary condition is vacuous when the boundary is empty.
Assume countable choice. An h-cobordism of dimension n+1 ≥ 6 with closed simply connected n-dimensional faces and connected total space is diffeomorphic to M₀×[0,1] relative to M₀.

Assume countable choice. Under the Morse cancellation criterion, every interior neighbourhood U of the closed unique connecting trajectory admits a critical-point-free replacement function and strictly descending replacement field, unchanged near the slab faces, with the field equal to the original outside a compact subset of U. Equality of the functions outside U is not asserted.

concerns.concern: F1 says 'transverse representatives are obtained by isotopy', and Step 1.1 uses that assertion. Its cited matrix definition explicitly says that it asserts no existence theorem for an arbitrarily small embedding isotopy; the cited relative-chain proof computes coefficients after transversality rather than constructing that isotopy. The missing justification is short: a finite parameter family of small ambient perturbations, parametric transversality, and compact-source embedding openness give the required isotopy. Supply or cite that argument rather than attributing it to the matrix definition.

The Definition asserts 'After an arbitrarily small isotopy of the attaching data ... are transverse'. Its declared intersection-number suppliers provide transverse map representatives, while the earlier attaching-belt definition expressly withholds a small embedding-isotopy existence theorem. The assertion is standard, but this additional embedding-preserving transversality step is not supplied by the cited definitions. The same short finite-parameter ambient perturbation argument identified for the homology lemma would justify it.

alerts.finding: F2 restates the owned elimination lemma as applying when 'a framed sphere in the outgoing boundary after the q-handles meets the belt sphere ... and is isotopic one level higher to a trivial embedding'. The current Statement of lem-handle-elimination-by-trading-a-pair additionally requires the full attaching region to lie in the common part obtained by deleting the existing upper attaching tubes, restricts 1 ≤ q ≤ n−2, and requires framed isotopy to a standard trivial embedding. F2 omits these qualifications. Steps 1.1–2.1 do construct common-part framed data, so this alert concerns the inaccurate supplier restatement rather than asserting failure of those applications.

F2 attributes the assertion that an upper attaching sphere supplies the 'i-th column of the intersection matrix' to both def-based-handle-chain-complex-over-the-fundamental-group-ring and def-middle-handle-intersection-matrix-of-an-h-cobordism. The former fixes the intended group-ring column convention. The latter is specifically a simply connected integral definition with upper handles in rows, lower handles in columns, and differential x ↦ xM on row coordinates; its column-coordinate matrix is Mᵀ. Thus the second citation does not supply the stated general group-ring column convention. The first citation does supply it, making this a citation/convention clarification.

seams_checked.note: Checked handle definitions, full attaching-isotopy extension, disjoint reordering, CW models and disk absorption. Relative comparisons retain the incoming face and transport later data; actual incoming CW structures are distinguished from models.

Finiteness and Morse evaluation use the finite handle complex and the Morse Euler identity with their closed-manifold and coefficient hypotheses. Full AC is explicitly supplied where excellent Morse-function existence requires it.

Checked tangent-first normal orientation, ordered zero-section/graph signs, signed Euler evaluation and mod-two zero counts. The Euler corollary explicitly supplies the admissible-base and numerability hypotheses.
Existence, self-indexing, duality and simultaneous low/high elimination preserve the stated collar-extension meaning of completeness and complementary reverse indices.

The closed-manifold, field-valued coefficient supplier is used as a local calculation, with the integral relative-triad argument reconstructed explicitly in prop-relative-handle-chain-complex-of-a-cobordism. Row coordinates and the transpose convention are stated.

Opened the outgoing-boundary disk-factor lemma and full-dimensional isotopy-extension lemma. Uses concern actual framed tubes, belt spheres and their complements; boundary-source disk tubes are constructed separately.

Stable moves retain both sheet dimensions ≥3. The two-dimensional cases establish complement injection for actual handle belts, including the reversed endpoint. Compared the borderline construction with [Milnor, Theorem 6.6 and proof](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/surgery/hcobord.pdf), printed pp. 71–84.

The actual item citation is the positive-basis path-connectivity lemma, used to close the oriented rank-four framing around the attaching circles. No Pontryagin-Thom classification strengthening is used.

Checked connected-sum descent, oriented class identification and the seven-sphere homeomorphism route. Product uses have closed simply connected faces, total dimension at least six, and countable choice; orientation preservation follows from fixing the oriented incoming face.

The clutching-degree lemma uses the boundary-degree identity for a nonzero boundary field, which the supplier actually states without requiring outwardness. The application is four-dimensional and uses matching base/fibre orientations.

Checked reduced-degree uses, local displacement perturbations, Euler finiteness and tangent-family signs. The fixed-point displacement id−f_t contributes (−1)^n for positive-time families tangent to X; the Poincare-Hopf recovery uses a family tangent to −X.

The boundary-coefficient lemma preserves endpoint conventions and explicitly limits use of the matrix definition to its middle range. Product charts and core-normal/belt orientation comparisons are used with the stated ordered intersection sign.

Read the citing page and checked its item references. No direct citation to an owned handle-calculus item was found on this A page; the declared page prerequisite introduces no stronger cancellation or slide assertion.

Most uses preserve the symmetric h-cobordism definition and actual-belt complement hypotheses. Two restatements need clarification: the two-index normal-form lemma's F2 omits common-part/range/full-framing qualifications of the elimination supplier, and the group-labelled Whitney lemma's F2 cites the integral row-coordinate middle-matrix definition for a group-ring column convention. Both are routed in alerts; their proofs also contain the relevant common-part construction or correct group-ring supplier.

Checked the framing, general-position and adapted-tube consumers. They use complementary transverse product charts locally and do not infer disk cleanliness or extendibility of an arbitrary prescribed frame from that chart lemma.
